items.t: Chapter 10 (al-bāb al-ʿāshir): On the secrets of the Fātiḥa and its renowned occult properties and invocations [110]

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that whoever has a need and desires that it be fulfilled, let him be assiduous in the recitation of these names and of the supplication, for it will be fulfilled, if God, exalted is He, wills. And before that, let it be that you pray two rakʿas. Then, when you have finished your prayer, you say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. My Lord, I ask You by that whereby You opened the world of the unseen, by the self-disclosure unto the Real, which manifests the cause of the sending down, and by the One transcendent in command, in existence, in hiddenness, and in the intelligible — that being a thing of the senses for whomever You have aided, nay, a thing known to whomever You have granted witnessing, nay, a thing unknown to whomever You will. Whatever of it is ambiguous is a multiplicity that does not impugn the oneness of what You have made firmly established of the firmly established [revelation]. O ʿAlīm (All-Knowing), O Ḥakīm (All-Wise), O Fattāḥ (Opener), O Allāh, O Lord! I ask You, O God, by the secret of the relation that binds together the Presence of Necessity and [the Presence of] Contingency — the relation that requires the manifestation of the Greatest Attribute by the undetermined Name, for the establishing of the divine realities, in general and in particular, at the outset and at the return, out of the amplitude of the all-embracing scope of the All-Merciful nature (raḥmāniyya), which has no end — [I ask You by] the settled abiding of the [visionary] event, unto the witnessing of the fixity of him who is brought near by the nearness whose quiddity is unknown of Him. O Raḥmān (All-Merciful), O Raḥīm (Compassionate), O Fattāḥ, O ʿAlīm! I ask You for illumination, for glad tidings, for aid within [Your] decree, for triumph, for preservation, for protective care, for covering, for perfecting, for wholesome provision, for blessing, for hope, for a good opinion of You, and for despair of all besides You. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate — a coming-to-be by Your command, a perfecting by Your munificence, and a blessing from You. Blessed is Your name, and exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You. In You we have believed, upon You we rely, and to You we have submitted. I ask You by Your light, O Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4): illumine our sights by Your light, O Light of light, O Guide of the misguided — there is no guide but You! Guide us upon the straight path (Q 1:6). Make us independent of all besides You through Yourself, O Ghanī (Self-Sufficient), O Mughnī (Enricher), O Allāh — [make us] witnesses unto You, O Raḥmān. "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). O God, I ask You by the fact that You are God in the realities of pure specification, and by the fact that You are God, the like of whom there is nothing, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (Q 42:11). I ask You to bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad, and to fulfil my need, by the right of the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:7). I ask You to bestow favour upon me by the fulfilment of my need and of all my needs entirely, and of whatever holds for me the good of this world and of the hereafter, [I being] preserved by [Your] protective care, preserved from calamities by the special properties of the [ultimate] ends. /fol. 56v./ O You who return again and again with good things, O You who are in truth the One worthy to be feared and worthy to forgive and the Possessor of good deeds — do not make us of the people of disgrace in this world and in the next, and make us of those who are not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:7). O God, do not make us to go astray nor to lead astray, nor to be driven from Your door, nor to despair of Your face — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

And this is another supplication by means of the noble Sūrat al-Fātiḥa. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 1:1–2) — a praise that shall be for me an [occasion of] good pleasure and a loan [laid up] with the Lord of the worlds. The All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 1:3), who spread out the climes, and chose Moses as [His] interlocutor, and gives life to the bones when they are decayed, and named Himself the All-Merciful, the Compassionate — for they are two generous, noble names, a healing for every malady and for every sick man. Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4), who has in [His] dominion no contender, no peer, no vizier, and no counsellor; rather He was before the existence of all the worlds entirely. You are my encompassment and my defence against all the satans, my help against those far off and those near at hand, and my direction against the differing kinds. You alone we worship (Q 1:5) — with acknowledgement; and we are ashamed of [our] sins, and we confess [our] shortcoming, and we ask Your forgiveness for all sins, faults, and defects, and we turn to You in repentance. And we bear witness that there is no god but God alone, having no associate, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His messenger. O Allāh, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour) — You alone, having no associate, no modality, no rival, and no likeness. And I bear witness that our master Muḥammad is Your servant and Your messenger, God bless him and grant him peace. And You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5) — by You, in every need, and against every obstinate adversary, and in every affair among the affairs of this world and of religion. O Guide of the misguided, there is no guide but You! Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:6–7), of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous — and how excellent are these as companions!(Q 4:69). In the name of God, Lord of the first and of the last, Creator of whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth, Raiser-up of the prophets and the messengers and the believers, in truth; Powerful, Majestic, Deliverer, Compassionate; one Lord in [all] the worlds, the Worshipped in every place, the One declared one by every tongue, the Excellent, the Eternal, the Consummate, the Fashioner, the Subduer of His creation all together. Quddūs (All-Holy) — 3 times — He before whom necks are abased and to whom the lofty, towering [mountains] have submitted. And faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting; and he who bears wrongdoing has failed (Q 20:111). O Ḥayy (Living), O Qayyūm (Self-Subsisting), O Muqaddim (Advancer), O Muʾakhkhir (Deferrer), O Awwal (First), O Ākhir (Last), O Ẓāhir (Manifest), O Bāṭin (Hidden), O Wālī (Governor), O Mutaʿālī (Most Exalted), O Barr (Benign), O Tawwāb (Ever-Relenting), O Muntaqim (Avenger), O ʿAfū (Pardoner), O Raʾūf (Ever-Gentle), O Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion), O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām! Ḥayyūm Ayyūm Qāʾim Qayyūm Dāʾim Dayyūm. Truly, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest (Q 13:28). O Ḥayy, O Qayyūm, You see me and You hear my speech, my humble entreaty, and my complaint. You are my goal, my request, and my hope, and I am the one in need of You. And You are the Knower of the secret and of the whispered converse; nothing in the earth nor in the heaven is hidden from You. You are the Lord of the noble Throne, and the One who has encompassed everything in knowledge and numbered everything in count. I ask You for beneficial bounty, for an upright religion, for a certainty /fol. 57r./ that is truthful, and for a far-reaching wisdom. O Qayyūm, Yāh Yāh, Yā Hū Yā Hū! I ask

You for the lifting of the veil of the unseen, with all that is within it, that I may behold the abiding Spirit. Āh Āh Āh. You — Yā Hū, O Ḥayy, O Qayyūm, O Light of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the mighty Throne! I ask You to bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad and his companions, and to grant peace; and to unveil for me the secrets of Your names; and to subject to me all Your creation in obedience, and my heart to You in worship; and to provide for me, and to show me the lights of Your guidance and the knowledge of Your secrets, that I may be made joyful by the dazzling [splendour] of what appears of Your gentle subtlety, O Laṭīf (Subtle) of the subtle, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Then you ask for what you desire of the affairs of this world and of the hereafter, and your need will be fulfilled, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted.
*And this too is the invocation of the blessed Fātiḥa, its spiritual discipline (riyāḍa), and the compelling formula (zajr) of the invocation. So understand.*

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that when you desire the operation and the occupying of yourself with this blessed invocation, then withdraw alone into a place that is pure and clean, and pray the five prayers at their [proper] times. Then you recite the noble Fātiḥa after each prayer 18 times, and that for a period of 14 days, while you are pure in intention. Then, when you have finished your prayers, invoke with these invocations. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 1:1–2) — the Illuminator of the inner sights of the gnostics with the lights of gnosis and of certainty; the Attractor of the imams of all the verifiers with the attractions of nearness and of empowerment; the Opener of the locks of the hearts of those who profess [His] oneness with the keys of the divine oneness, and their Attractor with the attractions of the nobility of the manifest opening; who made excellent everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of a base fluid (Q 32:7–8); the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, the All-Wise, the High, the Mighty, the Beginningless, the Eternal, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing; who wrote the signs of the divine oneness with the pens of power upon the breasts of the people of empowerment and of instruction, and traced the lines of the people of guidance upon the scrolls of gnosis for the people of sainthood — and sufficient for you [as witness] are the Companions of the Cave and al-Raqīm. He addressed Moses, the one spoken to, with the speech of honouring, and ennobled His noble Prophet with honouring and with ennobling: And We have indeed given you seven of the oft-repeated, and the mighty Qurʾān (Q 15:87). Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4), the Shatterer of the tyrants and of the rebellious, the Destroyer of the transgressing oppressors, the Shatterer and Crusher of the heads of the pharaohs, the Overturner of the banners of the people of innovation and of the heretics. That is God, your Lord; so blessed be God, Lord of the worlds (Q 40:64). O You who adorned the engendered beings with the garments of engendering, and sent forth the choice mounts of the dominion-realities to take refuge [in] the led coursers of firm generosity! O You who spread the clouds of His pardon over the whole of creation, all together! O You who has no associate in His dominion and no helper! You alone we worship (Q 1:5) — confessing our incapacity to fulfil the right of Your worship; and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5) — in what You have commanded, namely the fulfilling of Your rights at every time and season. O Possessor of the mighty triumph! /fol. 57v./ O Possessor of the all-pervading bounty! O You who gives life to the bones when they are decayed! Guide us upon the straight path (Q 1:6) — the path of the people of the upright religion; the path of the people of rectitude and of uprightness; the path of those upon whom You have gazed with the eye of Your providential care; the path of those who are the people of resolve and of sound wayfaring; the path of the people of [noble] character and of submission; the path of those who held fast to guidance and rejoiced in what was with them. The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:7) of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous — and how excellent are these as companions!(Q 4:69) not those against whom there is wrath (Q 1:7). Bestow upon us from Yourself the gifts of the truthful; and make us witness the witnessing-places of the martyrs and of the righteous; and supply us from Yourself with the angels of victory and of certainty; and grant us operative disposal among the engendered beings, the dominion-realities, and engendering. And do not make us to go astray nor to lead astray, nor to be driven from Your door; and do not gather us into the throng of those who go astray (Q 1:7). The invocation is complete.

And this is its adjuration and its compelling formula (zajr). You say: O you spiritual spirits, possessors of the luminous essences, made resplendent by the All-Merciful favours and by the Lordly laws (nawāmīs), you who stand [charged] with the operative deployment of the subtleties of the letters and of their hidden fine points, you who are appointed over the subjugation of the spiritual spirits — the spiritual force of the numbers — and over the knowings of their treasured secrets: answer, O mighty spirits and noble angels — Jibraʾīl, and Mīkāʾīl, and Isrāfīl, and ʿAzrāʾīl, and Rūqiyāʾīl! Take charge of the service of him who calls upon you, and be for him a help and helpers. The answering is due to God and to His messenger. Ahyā Sharāhiyā Adūnāy Aṣbāʾūt Āl Shadāy Tashīm. Understand my intent, and fulfil my needs, and undertake my service, by the right of God, al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), al-Razzāq (the Provider), al-Ḥakīm (the All-Wise), al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-ʿAlī (the High)

By pious reverence toward God, exalted is He, and by the keeping of your secret, you will attain your desire; and know the worth of what has come to you. And the suffumigation for this invocation is everything of sweet fragrance, such as — [the edition's text is dislocated here: the list of incenses that "such as" governs stands below, beginning "aloeswood of Qumār"; what follows as far as "and [His blessing be] upon you" is a displaced block, itself beginning in mid-sentence] — upon that. And if you are upright with him, then he will be upright with you, and he will charge one of his servant-spirits (khuddām) with you, and it will fulfil for you whatever you desire of your needs. And you must let him take the covenant upon you and lay down conditions upon you, among them that you shall not lie, nor eat what is unlawful, nor do anything of the acts of disobedience. And if you enter into covenant with him on the last night of the 14, a great green bird will come to you and will stand before you; and do you be the first to greet it with peace, for it is a mighty king. And deploy it in whatever you desire, after: "al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), al-Ilāh (the God), al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great); Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), Ḥā-Mīm (Q 42:1), ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:2). Answer, O Green King! May God bless you, and [His blessing be] upon you." And when there is — [the dislocated incense list resumes here, governed by "such as" above] aloeswood of Qumār (al-qumārī), benzoin (jāwī), nadd, mastic, and raw ambergris if it be possible, and everything he wishes, all of it among the things of sweet fragrance. And peace.

And there follows it, likewise, a third invocation for this noble sura. If you desire love and affection from a king or a governor who has turned against you, you fast on Thursday and on Monday, and you recite this invocation at your breaking of the fast 15 times, and at dawn the like of it. And you supplicate, asking God, exalted is He, for the turning of his heart toward you, and that He make him well-disposed to loving you; and you name him by your name. For you will see a /fol. 58r./ mighty secret in the swiftness of the answer and in the affection and love [that come] from him — whether he be a sultan or an obstinate tyrant, he will be abased and will submit to you, if God, exalted is He, wills. And if you desire the fulfilment of a need from among people, then fast on Thursday, then withdraw apart, and multiply the recitation of it in the manner that is for love, with presence of heart and gathered thought: your need will be fulfilled swifter than lightning. And its spiritual discipline (riyāḍa) is 9 days, or 7. And write, together with Sūrat al-Fātiḥa, a noble wafq, square in form, which is 9,360, without the basmala, for affection and love. And you set the square before you and recite the invocation 15 times, as has been mentioned, at the breaking of the fast; and you suffumigate the square with sweet incense in the depth of the night [Fig. 27] and you apportion it in stages until dawn. Then you set the square before you and recite the conjuration (ʿazīma) 15 times. Then you take up the blessed square and carry it: your affairs will prosper in all that you seek, if God, exalted is He, wills, and the spiritual beings will serve you through the blessing of Sūrat al-Fātiḥa, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of the square. [Wafq of 9,360: cells as in the source — ] And this is the aforementioned invocation > you say < the invocation of Sūrat Fātiḥat al-Kitāb. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 1:2) — with a praise that surpasses [all], the most perfect of it and the most beautiful of it, among all created beings. And I plunge into the sea of the light of that praise with a plunging that envelops me, outwardly and inwardly, with might, with awe-inspiring dignity, and with empowerment, until the Day of Judgement; and I hold fast to it with a preservation that encompasses me and guards me from all who harm and all who lead astray — a praise that shall be for me good pleasure, and a loan [laid up], and preservation, and relief, and a wealth with which I shall stand in need of no one of the first or of the last; and that shall be for me a mercy and a might by which I am made mighty, until by it I abase the assault of every tyrant. The All-Merciful (Q 1:3), whose mercy encompasses all things, so that every existent bears witness to it and to what has been confirmed to it of His beneficence; for everything has its beginning from it and within it, in secret and in open, and its final end is unto it, secretly and openly. I ask You by this secret which You have made manifest and which was plain to the eye, that You plunge me into its sea with a plunging that shall not depart from me at all times and seasons; and that it be for me a support and a provision after which I shall stand in need of nothing in any time or place, and a shield with which I am singled out amid the wiles of mankind and jinn. The Compassionate (Q 1:3), who has shown me gentle kindness by that which came to me beforehand from Him of mercy and mighty bounty — so that that mercy and that bounty were foregoing from Him unto me in the ancient pre-eternity, and here am I turning about within them both ever since I came to be, in knowledge and in creation, with the most wondrous influx and the most delightful bliss. I ask You, O my Master, /fol. 58v./ for the lavishing of Your blessing and the perpetuity of Your favour, by Your foregoing mercy, so that I shall fear no plot from any base schemer; and that You purify me, in creation and in character, from every blameworthy quality. Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4), whose affair is too magnificent for Him to stand in need of a partner or the aid of a helper, and who has subdued all who are in the kingdom and in the dominion by His power that crushes all the tyrants and all the arrogant — severe in assault against the transgressing wrongdoers, the Subduer, unremitting in His strength and His subjugation and His assault against whoever rebels and transgresses among all the arrogant tyrants and the transgressors and the rebels, the Shatterer of whoever associates himself with Him in His magnificence and His grandeur, so that from His punishment and the severity of His seizing he becomes a perisher among those who perish. I ask You that You subject to me the heart of So-and-so, O Musakhkhir al-qulūb (Subjector of hearts); and that You incline it, O Muʿaṭṭif (the One who inclines); and that You make it tender, O Ḥannān (the Tenderly Compassionate); and that You soften it, O Mulayyin (the Softener), even as You softened the iron for David — peace be upon him — Badūḥ, marrāt ("times"), Daḥūb and Daḥab. O Master of the kings of all the worlds entire, give me possession of the forelock of So-and-so son of So-and-so, and of his heart and his body, until he be in my grasp among the abased. There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87). My Lord, deliver me from distress, and let Your mercy overtake me, O Most Merciful of the merciful. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5). I have laid You up in store for my poverty and my destitution; there is no god but You. O You before whose magnificence the tyrants and the arrogant are humbled, and before whose majesty the transgressors of mankind and jinn and the arrogant and the rebellious are made small! O Severe in assault, O Mighty in subjugation, O Avenger who takes vengeance upon every possessor of entrenched violence! Strengthen me with Your help, and with a help from You and a manifest victory, that I may subdue my enemies among mankind and jinn entire. I ask You, my God, by what You have made manifest of the fire of Your subjugation, that You inflict loss upon them, so that they turn back as losers; and that You guide me to Your straight path — the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:7). Amen. And upon whom You have gazed with the eye of Your providential care; the path of those who held fast to right guidance and rejoiced in what was with them. The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:7). Bestow upon us from Your presence the gifts of the truthful; and make us witness the witnessing-places of the martyrs and of the righteous; and supply us from Yourself with the angels of victory and of certainty and of empowerment, even as You have said that in Your clear Book, sent down upon Your Prophet, the Messenger: Your Lord will supply you with three thousand angels sent down. Yes — if you are steadfast and pious, and they come upon you of a sudden, your Lord will supply you with five thousand angels, marked out (Q 3:124–125). And grant us operative disposal among the engendered beings, the things brought into being, and engendering. And pour out upon us, O God, from the effusion of Your bounties and Your favours, blessings that shall bring back upon us something of the blessings of religion; and do not make us to go astray nor to lead astray, nor to be driven from Your door; and do not gather us into the throng of the unbelievers and of the insolent who go astray. I ask You, O God, O Succour of those who seek succour: succour me! — you recite it 7 times — And reach me, O God, with Your subtle kindness, hidden and concealed; for truly, whomever You have hidden beneath the hiddenness of Your subtle kindness, hidden and concealed, is indeed hidden, and healed, and pardoned, and sufficed, and fulfilled. /fol. 59r./ There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87) — you recite it 7 times — and fulfil my need in such-and-such a matter. His command, when He desires a thing, is only that He say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything (Q 36:82–83). [I adjure] you by the might of God's might, and by the light of the Face of God, and by the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and the Book of God, and by that which the Pen has run with from God — that you answer and hasten! Ashhat, Ashhat, al-Yaqsuṭ: quickly, in haste! O Ḥaymūn, and O Ḥamdān: quickly! O Samdān: quickly, in haste! Take charge of the disquieting of So-and-so [...]. I adjure [You by] Your mercy which encompasses all things: and relieve me of every anguish, O Reliever of the distressed; relieve me by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Shahath. And reach me within Your concealment — the ample, the fortified, the impregnable, the sufficing, the preserving, the veiling, the all-encompassing ... and plunge me into the amplitude of Your provision, from the treasuries — and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:83). 7 times.

And know — may God grant me and you success — that the secrets of the noble Fātiḥa have wondrous occult properties, even as the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever recites it when he lays his side upon the bed, and recites with it Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1) 3 times and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān), is secured from everything except death.)) And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — that he said: al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — fell ill, and the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — was grieved; so God, exalted is He, revealed to him: Recite a sura in which there is no fāʾ — for the fāʾ is of the afflictions (āfāt) — over a vessel in which there is water, 40 times, and you wash with it his hands, his feet, his face, his head, and what is inward and what is outward of his body; for God, exalted is He, will take away from him what pains him, if God, exalted is He, wills. And some of the scholars said: whoever writes [readingfor the edition's] the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in a clean vessel and effaces it with water, and a sick man drinks of it, he is healed, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and the recitation of it, God, exalted is He, purifies his inward being of all the afflictions of the soul and the satanic incursions. And whoever writes it in a glass bowl and effaces it with pure balsam oil, and breaks his fast upon the oil, 70 times, and one afflicted with sciatica (ʿirq al-nasā) or with pain of the back is anointed with it — that is lifted from him; and it is, by the aid of God, exalted is He, of benefit against the wind-ailment (al-rīḥ) and against hemiplegia (al-fālij), and against all cold and moist illnesses, spiritual and corporeal. And whoever writes the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in a vessel of gold in the first hour of the day of Friday, with musk and saffron and camphor, and effaces it with rose-water and puts it in a phial — then, when he wishes to enter the presence of a king or a governor, and wipes his face with it, he attains acceptance and love with the one upon whom he enters. And whoever enters upon one whose evil he fears, and recites the Fātiḥa, is secured from his evil, by the leave of God, exalted is He.
Ibn Abī al-Shaʿbī complained of pain in the flank [reading

the edition's ,]and it was said to him: Keep to the foundation of the Qurʾān, which is the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb; for I heard Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — say /fol. 59v./: Everything has a foundation; the foundation of the Qurʾān is the Fātiḥa, and the foundation of the Fātiḥa is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". So when ... and you fall ill, keep to the Fātiḥa: you will be healed, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And the erudite scholar Ibn al-Qayyim said in his book: Every malady has a remedy, and the best of treatment is with the Fātiḥa, for which I have found ... ... ... in healing. And that is because I remained for a time at Mecca, a malady befalling me, and I could find no physician at all, nor any remedy. So I said: Let me treat myself with the Fātiḥa. And I did that, and I was healed. And I did that for one who complained of a severe pain — and I see in it a wondrous efficacious influence.

And I used to send that to whoever complained of a severe pain, and many of them would recover swiftly, by the leave of God, exalted is He, through the blessing of the Fātiḥa. The scholars who know God have said: whoever recites "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" 19 times upon entering the presence of a tyrant — God, exalted is He, secures him from his evil. And whoever writes it according to the number of its letters in the first hour of Friday is preserved from the assaults of men and jinn. And in a sound report: whoever says every day, 3 times, "In the name of God, the best of names; in the name of God, Lord of the earth and the heaven; in the name of God, with whose name nothing in the earth or in the heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" — God, exalted is He, secures him from sorcery, from poison, and from sickness, and suffices him against the evil of the sudden strokes of the night and of the day. Some of the scholars have said: whoever writes the letters with which the openings of the suras are opened in a glass bowl, and effaces it with rainwater, and one who has been poisoned drinks it — he is secured from his illness, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((No one sets the Throne Verse upon property or upon a house and then has a satan draw near it, by the leave of God, exalted is He.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever recites the Throne Verse before going out from his dwelling — nothing of the afflictions touches him until he returns.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever places his hand upon his head and says He is God, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 59:22), to the end of the sura — it is for him a healing from every disease save death.)) And al-Masʿūdī said: it has reached me that whoever recites Sūrat al-Fatḥon the first night of the month of Ramaḍān in a supererogatory prayer — God, exalted is He, preserves him in that year from mishaps. And the shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn al-Suhrawardī said: I have heard that the recitation of [Sūrat] al-Burūj in the afternoon prayer is a healing from boils. And whoever writes the Fātiḥa and effaces it with water, and mixes that water into anything whatever — its blessing appears plainly to the eye. As for its effects in the letter-based mode (al-ṭawr al-ḥarfī): whoever recites it, after understanding the meanings of its letters, over a glass bowl with water in it, and drinks it upon a fast of 25 days — God opens for him a door of subtle kindness (luṭf), outwardly and inwardly. And in it also there is [something] for the subduing of tyrants: whoever writes [it], after a purification and a fast of 5 days, together with /fol. 60r./ the Verse of Creation — which is His word, exalted is He, Indeed your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days (Q 7:54), to the end of the verse — upon pure parchment on Friday while the preacher is upon the pulpit, and hangs it upon his head: God brings into being for him subtle kindness, and brings into being for him a trembling in hearts and in legs, and of necessity he cannot be withstood. And in it is a subtle secret for one whose forgetfulness is great, if he employs it in drinking. And if he writes it and places it in a house, no noxious creature that does harm enters it. And whoever writes it under a particular ascendant, for the inclining of hearts — for what is intended by the ascendant, in the view of those who practise astronomical observation, is a spiritual power for it; and if the heart's power of faith — I mean the psychic power — is found to be manifest, it is more effective than the ascendant, and stronger. Do you not see the corporeal receptivities in their world, how they were the more effective? And this comes about only for one who has an understanding of the secrets of the letters. And beware of ritual impurity in anything of that, whether it be numerical or letter-based, and you will find its good fortune. And God, exalted is He, knows best. And this is its form.

And among His names is al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), which God, exalted is He, sent down in four places. In Sūrat al-Anʿām, His word, exalted is He: Sight does not attain Him, but He attains all sight, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware (Q 6:103). This verse is of benefit to one who fears for himself from an enemy, a wrongdoer, or a tyrant: let him multiply His name al-Laṭīf, morning and evening, 129 times, reciting after it the verse mentioned. The second is in Sūrat Yūsuf: whoever fears a hardship, a tribulation, a straitness, a distress, a worry, or a grief — let him make remembrance of the name [Fig. 28] al-Laṭīf 129 times, saying after it Indeed my Lord is subtle toward what He wills; indeed He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise (Q 12:100). God, exalted is He, delivers him from the hardship, the tribulation, the worry, and the grief, and God, exalted is He, provides him with abundant dominion, with sovereignty, and with might. The third is in Sūrat Ḥā-Mīm ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf: whoever has had this world slip away from him, and has grown poor and needy of what is in people's hands — let him multiply, morning and evening, the name al-Laṭīf 129 times, and say after it God is subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty (Q 42:19). God, exalted is He, provides him with much good in abundance, and this world comes to love him despite itself, even if he does not desire it. The fourth is in the sura Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1): whoever is a seeker of investiture with office and of high posts, from [lacuna in the edition] /fol. 60v./ a seeker of [lacuna] or the like of that — let him multiply the recitation of al-Laṭīf by the number mentioned, and let him recite His word, exalted is He, Does He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware (Q 67:14).

Let us return to what we were about, concerning the benefits of the blessed and noble Fātiḥa. If it is written and effaced with rainwater, and the sick man wipes his face and his hands with it once, and drinks that water 3 times, and says at that > he says < "Heal — You are the Healer; suffice — You are the Sufficer; grant well-being — You are the Granter of well-being" 3 times, he is healed, so long as his appointed term has not come. And if one in whose heart there is a palpitation of the heart and a trembling drinks of that water, it subsides by the leave of God, exalted is

He, and the pain departs from him. And if it is written with musk and saffron in a vessel of glass and washed off with rose-water, and one who has an ailment drinks it, he is healed; or if the dull-witted child drinks the whole of it for 7 days on an empty stomach, his dullness departs from him and he retains what he hears, if God, exalted is He, wills. And if it is written with musk in a vessel of glass and effaced with the rainwater that falls in the month of Kānūn (December–January), and Iṣfahānī kohl is ground with it, and one weak of sight applies it as kohl, it polishes his sight, preserves the health of his eye, and removes its diseases. And if to that are added the gall of a white cock with a cleft comb (afraq) and the gall of a black hen, and someone applies it as kohl, he sees the spiritual figures (al-ashkhāṣal-rūḥāniyya), and they address him concerning what he did not know. And whoever persists in reciting it by night and by day, it removes from him sloth and failure, by the leave of God, exalted is He, and no pain of his eyes comes upon him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if the Fātiḥa is written in a pure, clean vessel and effaced with rose-water and dripped into the aching ear, it is cured of the pain, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if it is written with pure oil and recited over that oil 70 times, it subdues the wind-ailment (al-rīḥ) and hemiplegia (al-fālij); and if the sick man is anointed with it, he is cured of everything he suffers. And in it are benefits beyond counting, and it has a mighty effect in [procuring] love and in setting things right. And among its benefits: whoever has a need [to be met] by God, exalted is He, and desires His kindly inclination toward him — let him recite it in due order and with measured chanting (tartīl), with faith and conviction, 7 times, facing the qibla, in a state of complete ablution, with presence of mind, after the afternoon prayer, [having prayed] two rakʿas and reciting in each rakʿa the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ3 times; and let him ask God, exalted is He, for his need. Whatever need it be, it is fulfilled, in whatever place he wishes, if God, exalted is He, wills. And if its practitioner recites it during the daytime, night does not fall before it is fulfilled; and if he recites it at night, morning does not come before his need is fulfilled, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And God provides for him: And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning (Q 2:212). And among what has been tried and proved sound is that whoever recites it between the dawn prayer and the evening 41 times, and keeps to that for 40 days without adding anything to it — God fulfils his need, whatever it may be, and God provides him with a righteous child, even were he barren. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. /fol. 61r./

And these verses are transmitted from the book Kanz al-murīdīn ("The Treasure of the Aspirants") of Ibn Sabʿīn, who transmitted them from the Imām ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — on the excellence of the noble Fātiḥa, and they are these:
If you are one who seeks provision, and the success of your aim from slave and from freeman, and to gain swiftly what you hope for, and to be safe from opposition and from treachery —
then [take to] the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, for in it there is, for what you have hoped, a secret — and what a secret!
Keep constantly to its study after the night prayer, and at the dawn prayer, and at the noon prayer, and at the afternoon prayer,
5 and after the sunset prayer of every night, up to ninety — you follow it with ten.

You will attain what you wish of might and of standing, of great awe-inspiring presence and of loftiness of rank, and a covering that the nights do not alter by any event of diminishment that comes to pass, and [divine] enabling, and a relief lasting continually, and you will be safe from the retribution of every evil, and you will have need of no one for anything, nor be stricken by anything hateful or harmful,

10 nor by nakedness, nor hunger, nor destitution, nor by the violent grip of one who holds prohibition and command, and you will live in ease throughout a long life, and live in fair estate throughout a long age, for if you do so, there will come to you one bringing what makes you independent of Zayd and of ʿAmr, and you will continue in fair estate at every time, and live in ease throughout a long life.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him — that the manner of the spiritual discipline (riyāḍa) of the Fātiḥa is that you go into devotional seclusion for it in a pure, dark place in which no one sees you but God, glorified and exalted; and you fast 3 days, the first of them Sunday; and you neither eat nor drink anything ensouled, nor anything that issues from an ensouled creature; and your breaking of the fast is upon barley bread and oil; and you do not fill your belly; and you recite the Fātiḥa after each prayer 100 times. And this is the supplication; you say: O Lord, admit me into the deep of the sea of Your oneness (aḥadiyya) and the surety of Your unicity (waḥdāniyya), that I may come forth to the decreeing of Your mercy, with upon my face the gleaming of nearness from the traces of Your all-mercifulness (raḥmāniyya), held in awe through Your awe, strong through Your strength, mighty through Your might. And clothe me in the robes of honour of might and of acceptance, and make smooth for me the smooth ways of union and of arrival, and crown me with the crown of honour, and join in love between me and Your beloved ones in the abode of this world and the abode of the Resurrection. O Master, before whom the necks of the tyrants have been humbled! O Master of this world and of the hereafter! baʿshaqī baʿshaqamī nabdakan nabdasan. God took Abraham as an intimate friend, and He spoke to Moses in [direct] speech, and He honoured /fol. 61v./ our master > peace, a word from a Compassionate Lord < with a signal honouring. "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). O Master of the Day of Judgement! You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:5–7). And after three days there will appear to you in the prayer-niche a tuft of carded cotton, and it swells until it fills the place; then it remains for a day; then there comes forth from beneath it a man who says to you, "Peace be upon you! What is your need?" Do not ask of him anything of this world; say to him rather: "I want from you the Name and the Seal", and stipulate with him brotherhood. And the recitation is to be thirty after the dawn prayer, thirty after the noon prayer, thirty after the afternoon prayer, and ten after the sunset prayer. And after the recitation you supplicate with this blessed supplication, one time. You say: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 1:2) — with a praise that shall stand as a loan to my credit with the Lord of the worlds. The All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 1:3) — who spread out the climes, and singled out Moses as [His] interlocutor, who gives life to the bones when they are decayed. For they are two noble and lofty names, a healing for every ailment and every sick man, a sufficiency for every destitute man, a road to the Gardens of Bliss, and a deliverance from the torment of Hellfire. Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4) — He has in His dominion no partner, no contender, no peer, and no helper. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5)

— we worship with acknowledgement, and we confess our shortcoming. And I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner; and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His messenger, whom He sent as a bearer of good tidings and a warner to the whole of creation entire, and to the whole body of the Muslims, and as a mercy to the believers. For You are God, the Bringer of [all] beings into being, the Knower of the hidden things of concealment, who wraps the night about the day, my proof before all the worlds and my orientation toward those near and those far and toward the differing kinds. And You alone we ask for help — [we seek] help of You in every need, of the affair of this world and of religion. O God, O Master of the kings of all the worlds entire! There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87). My Lord, deliver me! My Lord, overtake me with Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful, and deliver me from what I fear and guard against! O Benign One, enrich me, by the right of You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us upon the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:5–7). And after the second supplication of the spiritual discipline (riyāḍa) of the Fātiḥa, you recite the Fātiḥa after every prayer eighteen times, and after the witr prayer twenty-five times; and [then] there is no fasting and no discipline. But if you keep to the spiritual retreat (khalwa) for seven days together with the complete discipline, then you say after the supplication: "O God, subject to me Your servant al-Rafraf al-Akhḍar (the Green Rafraf) — truly You are powerful over every thing." And the suffumigation after the recitation is with aloeswood, frankincense, and good benzoin (jāwī), during the days of the retreat. And speak to no one: you will attain what is sought, and God, exalted is He, will subject to you what you seek, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And this is a love-procuring formula upon the noble Sūrat al-Fātiḥa. You say: /fol. 62r./ In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 1:1–2). Take charge, O Jibrīl, you and your servant-spirits (khuddām) and your helpers, by the right of God — al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Jabbār (the Compeller), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing). I ask you, O Jibrīl, that you cast the love of 202 son of 202 into the heart of 202, by the right of The All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 1:3). O Jawād (Munificent One), O Jamīl (Beautiful One)! Take charge, O Mīkāʾīl, hearing and obeying, and cast the love of 212 into the heart of 202. Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4). And by the right of God — al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Mājid (the Glorious) — take charge, O Isrāfīl, you and your helpers, and cast the love of 202 into the heart of 202. And by the right of God, al-Ḥayy, al-Qayyūm, and by the right of You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5), and by the right of al-Malik (the King), al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), al-Muqaddim (the Advancer), al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer): Guide us upon the straight path (Q 1:6). And by the right of God — al-Ḥayy, al-Qayyūm, al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge) — take charge, O Nūriyāʾīl, you and your helpers, and cast the love of 202 into the heart of 202, by the right of the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour (Q 1:7). And by the right of al-Wāḥid (the One), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Jawād (the Munificent), al-Karīm (the Generous) — take charge, O ʿAzrāʾīl, you and your helpers, hearing and obeying, and cast the love of 202 into the heart of 202, by the right of not those against whom there is wrath, nor those who go astray (Q 1:7). Amen. And by the right of al-Qāhir (the Subduer), al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Jalīl (the Majestic), al-Kabīr (the Great) — take charge, O Kasfiyāʾīl, you and your helpers, hearing and obeying, and cast the love of 202 into the heart of 202. They love them as God should be loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And this is the formula, and its form is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.
/fol. 62v./
Fig. 29

Fāʾida, for every illness. It is [related] of the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever has an illness in him, let him recite over water, each one seventy times, and drink it on an empty stomach: God, exalted is He, heals him of what is in him, if God, exalted is He, wills, by His gentleness, His beneficence, and His generosity.)) And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((The Mother of the Book is a healing from every disease.)) The gnostics of God, exalted is He, have said: in it are a thousand outward occult properties and a thousand inward occult properties. And whoever writes it in a clean vessel, washes it off with water, and gives it to a sick man to drink — his illness is lightened, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And he — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((When you lay your side upon the bed and recite the Fātiḥa of the Book and Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1), you are indeed secured from every thing.)) And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((… the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and he places his hand upon his head and recites the verse: he is healed of every disease save death (al-sām).)) And God, exalted is He, knows best.

Faṣl, in which I mention the Veil of the Lock, of majestic worth. You say: I have veiled myself with the might of al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), who is made mighty in the might of His might, by Ṭawīl Īl, Abhiyyīl, Daʿīl, Adūnāy, Aṣbāʾūt, Āl Shadāy, Aylūhīm. And truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76). God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). Guard, O Faqaj Makhmat! His word is the truth, and His is the dominion on the Day when the Trumpet is blown — Knower of the unseen and of the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the All-Aware (Q 6:73). And by the right of Ahyā Sharāhiyā: [guard me] from the evil of every satan and every rebel demon, and from the evil of every obdurate tyrant. By the right of Ṭalīkh Aṭwārīkh Ṭamāliyā: Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1) — I am sufficed; Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:1–2) — I am protected. By the right of /fol. 63r./ — O Ṣadaqiyāʾīl, and veil away from such-and-such [a person] what is upon him of spirits, and of fear, and of terror, and of the evil of the visitants of night and day, and of Mānish, Mamdūhīs, Karhīsh, Karhiyūsh, ʿAlashāqish, Aqshāmaqīsh. Descend, O spiritual spirits …! And you, O Ṣarfiyāʾīl, and you, and the satans and the hosts of Iblīs entire — Yaʿlaṭif Halṭaf Salmaṭīʿ Asmāṭūn Aṭʿīn Bimaʿkash Barqash Qafāyil Hūrab Maryūqad Qātish — and mankind, and the spiritual beings, and the terrestrial beings — Baṭrash Ṭarash — and by light, and by the name of God, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by the impregnable veil, against all the rebel demons of the jinn. … has been revealed …(Q 72:1) — to its end, up to His word — … outrageous falsehood (Q 72:4). And truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76). I have guarded my body, my hair, and my senses from the evil of the jinn. … a guardian (Q 86:4 — displaced: the closing word of the quotation of Q 86:1–4 below). And by those ranged in ranks, and the drivers driving, and the reciters of a remembrance (Q 37:1–3). By the star when it falls (Q 53:1). With Sūrat al-Qamar to its end (Q 54), and with the sura Say …(sura unidentified: a bare catchword in the source) — … the glorious (Q 50:1 — displaced: the closing word of the quotation of Q 50:1 below). Nūn. By the pen and what they inscribe (Q 68:1). And by the heaven and the night-comer! And what will make you know what the night-comer is? The piercing star! Truly over every soul there is [a guardian](Q 86:1–4). Yābat Yaskālaj Adnū Sārash — His help! Your Lord will reinforce you with noble angels — by Alif-Lām-Mīm (Q 2:1), Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād (Q 7:1), Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:1–2), Qāf. By the [glorious] Qurʾān (Q 50:1). Ḥal ʿAsaj Taḥāraṣaf Waṣafāt Baṭīsā Baṭamsiyā Baṭīsiyā ʿAlamsiyā Hayūsh ʿUrūsh Habash Mūkiyāhīl FayyāḍBarhamūdā Yāʿat. O servant-spirits of these names, take charge of such-and-such!

The Scroll of the Angels — peace be upon them. It is for protection: its bearer is in the safekeeping of God, exalted is He; and it wins great acceptance for whoever goes in with it to kings, sultans, and grandees. And following it is the hexagonal seal, the seal of the noble Fātiḥa: whoever carries it is divinely supported and given victory, and he subdues everyone who is hostile to him, and it is of benefit for all things entire. And these are the names: Huwa Huwa Yah Huwa Huwa Rah, and Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād; Ḥayy (Living), Aḥyā, Muḥyī (Giver of life), Mumīt (Bringer of death), Muḥtawī (Encompassing), Qādim (Coming), Qāʾim (Upholding), Qāhir (Subduing); Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf; Originator of the heavens and the earth; Badīʿ (Wondrous Originator), Rafīʿ (Exalted), Manīʿ (Impregnable), Samīʿ (All-Hearing). You are He beside whom there is no god; glory be to You — truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87). His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of every thing, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). God is the Creator of every thing, and He is Guardian over every thing (Q 39:62). Ṣād-Qāf-Nūn. God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). And you will not harm Him at all; truly my Lord is Guardian over every thing (Q 11:57). God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful (Q 12:64). Nay, it is a glorious Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:21–22). Mīṭaṭrūn Muḥīṭqalyāl Ṣaʿat Kaḥyāl Ṣaʿīkaʿīmahyāl. And this is the last of what has come down in the chapter on the noble, blessed Fātiḥa; and God knows best. And this is the form of the noble, blessed wafq, and it is as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills — glorified and exalted is He. And God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 63v./
